note: valid/link-corpus is one task per link construct — org labelled and unlabelled links, padded org url/label, bare URLs, the six trailing-punctuation classes, an unbalanced ')' next to a balanced one kept in the path, =verbatim= / ~code~ wrappers, the same url twice in both orders for dedupe, a jira-labelled host, a host matching two SYSTEMS rows, host fallback with the www. strip and downcasing, an unparseable ':port' url, scheme-only fragments, org internal links ([[My Heading]] / [[id:]] / [[file:]]), a non-web ftp: org link, and a link in the title ahead of two body-line links. The corpus previously held ONE link, so every one of those rules was unproven. The recorded `tasks links` / `--json` / `--system jira` output in the fixture README is the specification. Two residuals are NOT store-shaped and are deliberately not left as a fixtures_todo: (a) the SYSTEMS rows keyed to apex domains (github.com, slack.com, atlassian.net, linear.app, notion.so, docs.google.com, drive.google.com, figma.com, zoom.us) need those real hosts and the corpus is .invalid/example.com only by its own sanitization rule — the two rows that match on a host *label* (confluence., jira.) are covered here, along with every other branch of classify(); (b) shorthand expansion and custom system.<name> rows read $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tasks/config, which every fixture run points at an empty directory by corpus rule 3, so no store can carry them. Both are already covered by this slice's ruby_tests (test_classify_known_systems_and_fallback; the seven test_links_feature.rb shorthand cases and test_custom_system_rows_classify_self_hosted). Suggested oracle_gaps addition: 'Apex-domain SYSTEMS rows and config-driven shorthand/custom-system classification cannot be expressed as a store fixture (the corpus bans real hosts and pins XDG_CONFIG_HOME empty); they are proved by the unit oracle only, and the port needs unit tests for them rather than conformance cases.' Also worth recording in oracle_gaps: clean_bare's unbalanced-']' branch is unreachable from a bare URL, because BARE_URL excludes '[', ']', '"' and "'" from the match; it fires only on a shorthand value, i.e. config-only.

And add to **What was found while building this**, as a fourth numbered finding:

**4. Link dedupe prefers the *first* occurrence, not the labelled one.** `links-read`'s behavior sentence and `Links.extract`'s own comment ("first occurrence wins — it has the best label") both read as "the labelled form survives". It survives only when it appears first in the text: the org pass records offsets, the list is sorted by offset, and `uniq(&:url)` keeps the earliest. `valid/link-corpus` carries the same url in both orders — `11c00009` keeps its label, `11c00010` loses it — so an implementation of "prefer the labelled one" passes one and fails the other.

The § *Sanitization* table's URL row needs restating, since `link-corpus` adds roughly thirty. Replace:

| URLs | two, both on the reserved `example.invalid` TLD |

with:

| URLs | all on `example.invalid` or `example.com` (both reserved). `valid/link-corpus` holds ~30 of them, one per link construct; no real host appears anywhere in the corpus, which is why the built-in `SYSTEMS` rows keyed to apex domains are proved by unit test rather than by a fixture |

note: valid/deferred-tags is the corpus's first store built around Store::DEFER_TAG for the read path: an own hold, an own hold on a parent with an inherited-hold child and a grandchild held two levels up, an own hold on a WAITING task, a future-dated task with NO defer tag, and DONE / PROPOSED / archived records that still carry defer (the last three are unreachable by mutation — closing strips DEFER_TAG — so they exist to reach read-side branches nothing else in the corpus touches, and `check` passes on all of them). That set is what makes deferred_match? leave its pass-through branch on every arm: --someday, --deferred at open scope, --deferred at each non-open scope, --unavailable, and the two combinations. The recorded outcome pins the finding the slice most needs: --deferred means two different things by scope. At open scope it is exactly --unavailable, and it lists de000008, which is merely dated 2099 and carries no defer tag at all; at --done/--archived/--proposed/--all it drops to the literal tag test and returns the same set as --someday. --someday is the only spelling that always means the tag, and it excludes inherited holds. Suggested oracle_gaps addition: '--deferred is scope-dependent (open scope: any unavailability; non-open scope: the literal defer tag) and --someday is own-hold-only; valid/deferred-tags records both, and the two arms must be ported as separate rules rather than one predicate.' One more recorded behavior for the comparator's benefit: `tasks list +defer` returns nothing at the default scope even though +defer matches Item#tags, because the availability filter removes every held task first — a port that gets the conjunction order wrong produces output there and passes everywhere else in the corpus.

Add to the `valid/` index table, after the `link-corpus` row proposed above:

| `deferred-tags` | the `defer` hold: own, inherited two levels, and closed/proposed/archived carriers; the scope-dependent `--deferred` | 0 — `ok — 9 tasks parsed` (`--all-files`: 0 — `10 records`) |

And add to **What was found while building this**, as a sixth numbered finding (numbering follows the two proposed with `link-corpus` and `project-rollup-edges`):

**6. `--deferred` means two different things depending on scope.** At the default open scope it is a pure availability test — identical to `--unavailable`, and it lists a task that is merely dated in the future and carries no `defer` tag. At any non-open scope (`--done`, `--archived`, `--proposed`, `--all`) it drops to the literal `defer` tag test, where it returns exactly what `--someday` returns. `--someday` is the only spelling that always means the tag, and it reports own holds only — an inherited hold is an availability fact, not a tag fact. `valid/deferred-tags` records every arm.

note: The same fixture closes this slice's gap, and its README records the projection explicitly rather than only the CLI surface: TaskView#to_h against Representation.task for all nine records, showing `deferred` true/false, `available`, `availability_reason` and `availability_blocker_id`, next to the tags asymmetry the issue names — TaskView#tags keeps `defer` (de000003 -> ["defer", "@computer", "research"]) while Representation.task strips both `defer` and the @contexts (-> ["research"]). It also pins the reason ordering that only a defer-carrying closed record can prove: de000009 (DONE + defer) and de00000a (PROPOSED + defer) report `closed` and `proposed`, not `on_hold`, because build_availability short-circuits on source/state before the hold walk; and de000006 reports blocker de000004, the nearest deferred *ancestor*, not its parent de000005. Note for the port: bin/tasks `show --json` is a third projection again — it splits contexts out of tags but keeps `defer` in them — so three tag projections exist and the slice ports TaskView's.

note: valid/project-rollup-edges gives held_count its first non-zero value in the corpus and closes the three exclusion edges in one store: a project with an own-held task, a held parent and its inherited-hold child (held_count 3 against open_count 1 — the two halves of test_held_count_rolls_up_open_deferred_descendants and test_held_count_includes_inherited_hold); a project held end to end (open 0, held 2, still listed); an empty project; a done-only project; a project whose tasks sit inside a nested sub-section (which rolls up but is never listed in its own right); an area with open plus held work; and an area whose only open work is held. That last one is the fixture's sharpest edge and a finding: a held-only AREA disappears from `tasks projects` entirely and `tasks project show` on it answers `no match` with exit 2, because areas are gated on open_count.positive? while projects are listed unconditionally — the identical situation in a project (`Project held end to end`) is listed. Second finding worth an oracle_gaps line: held_count is JSON-only. Neither `tasks projects` nor `tasks project show` renders it, so a comparator restricted to the human surface cannot detect a wrong held_count at all; observable_outputs for this slice should name the --json envelope explicitly.
corpus_readme:
Add to the `valid/` index table, after the `link-corpus` and `deferred-tags` rows proposed above:

| `project-rollup-edges` | `held_count` over own and inherited holds, plus the empty / done-only / sub-section / held-only-area exclusion edges | 0 — `ok — 13 tasks parsed` |

And add to **What was found while building this**, as a fifth numbered finding:

**5. A held-only area is unreachable through the project surface.** `TaskQueries#projects` lists every section child of `Projects` unconditionally, but lists a top-level area only when its `open_count` is positive — and open work that is on hold does not count towards `open_count`. So an area whose only open task is deferred vanishes from `tasks projects`, and `tasks project show` on it answers `no match` with exit 2, while a *project* in the identical state is still listed. `valid/project-rollup-edges` carries both halves. Related: `held_count` appears in `--json` only, never in the human rendering, so the human surface cannot distinguish a project holding three parked tasks from one holding none.
